title: 20 portfolio About me references
method: Live desktop pages captured in Chrome and visually inspected. Descriptions paraphrase the pages; takeaways are design judgments. Layout groups describe the captured opening or subsection, not necessarily the full page. No mobile or interaction audit was performed.

examples.name: Mindy Nguyen
examples.label: One sentence + portrait
examples.image: A straightforward vertical portrait sits beside a large, brief introduction on a muted green background.
examples.copy: The opening identifies her discipline and current role in one sentence. Services and experience carry the detail below.
examples.takeaway: Give the personal introduction a clear job: establish who you are immediately, then let supporting sections supply proof.
examples.fit: Strong reference for a compact Moriz homepage section.

examples.name: Seán Halpin
examples.label: Arch portrait + friendly introduction
examples.image: A portrait in an arch-shaped frame balances a large introduction, with soft background color and generous space.
examples.copy: Role and location lead; a short career overview and current focus follow. Experience appears further down.
examples.takeaway: Use a distinctive portrait crop and a concise professional story to make the section feel personal without making it long.
examples.fit: Strong reference for warmth and an approachable image treatment.

examples.name: Lauren Hom / Hom Sweet Hom
examples.label: Classic portrait + conversational biography
examples.image: A tall studio portrait and a substantial text column share a pale mint background.
examples.copy: The biography moves from creative origins to teaching, hobbies, and food-related interests before a direct project enquiry.
examples.takeaway: Include one specific personal interest that connects naturally to the work you want to attract.
examples.fit: Useful writing reference; condense the longer biography for a homepage.

examples.name: Dennis Snellenberg
examples.label: Asymmetric portrait + client-facing description
examples.image: A large environmental portrait is paired with a much smaller text column and plenty of white space.
examples.copy: The description explains the service and approach to quality, while a larger positioning statement introduces the page.
examples.takeaway: A brief client-facing paragraph can do more work when the composition gives the image a strong presence.
examples.fit: Strong composition reference for Moriz’s combined design and development offer.

examples.name: Alice Lee / byalicelee
examples.label: Artist inside her creative world
examples.image: A colorful photo shows Alice surrounded by flowers and her own artwork, beside a warm cream biography panel.
examples.copy: The introduction states her practice and location, then names projects and creative interests as concrete evidence.
examples.takeaway: Photograph yourself with your work so the image communicates both personality and creative capability.
examples.fit: Strong reference if Moriz can use an authentic studio or work-in-progress photograph.

examples.name: Adham Dannaway
examples.label: Playful cutout + compact bio
examples.image: A cutout portrait looks toward the short introduction. Small personal photos sit beneath the opening composition.
examples.copy: Role, location, design approach, and off-duty interests fit into a short opening. Skills and longer stories follow separately.
examples.takeaway: Use the portrait’s gaze or pose to guide attention toward the words; keep the opening easy to scan.
examples.fit: Useful for combining professional clarity with a playful personal detail.

examples.name: Alice Seohyun Lee
examples.label: Working photograph + informal story
examples.image: A large candid-style image shows her working at a whiteboard, alongside a compact biography on white.
examples.copy: The text mixes geographic background, design education, agency experience, and hobbies. A humorous caption adds personality.
examples.takeaway: A working photograph can explain what collaboration with you feels like; a human caption can soften a restrained layout.
examples.fit: Useful for showing the person behind research, workshops, and design decisions.

examples.name: Kelsey O’Halloran
examples.label: Arched lifestyle photo + benefit-led bio
examples.image: A seated lifestyle portrait in an arch sits beside a serif introduction and two clear action links.
examples.copy: The personal introduction starts with a client benefit, then connects her journalism background to her research-based approach.
examples.takeaway: Connect personal background to a practical reason clients should care, then offer a direct route to work or services.
examples.fit: Strong copy structure for connecting Moriz’s research background to client outcomes.

examples.name: Lu Yu
examples.label: Speaking photograph + design philosophy
examples.image: A conference photograph and an offset text column sit on a charcoal background, with expressive typography around them.
examples.copy: An origin story about learning Chinese painting and calligraphy explains her attention to beauty, intention, and rationale.
examples.takeaway: Choose one formative story that explains how you think today, rather than listing a complete personal history.
examples.fit: Useful for an expressive editorial direction. Preserve readable contrast in any adaptation.

examples.name: Aarron Walter
examples.label: Drawn portrait + professional narrative
examples.image: A monochrome illustrated portrait appears against a blue painted accent on a dark page.
examples.copy: An accessible opening establishes a focus on human products; the longer biography supports it with leadership and project experience.
examples.takeaway: A commissioned portrait can express personality while keeping the surrounding layout restrained.
examples.fit: Useful alternative if a distinctive illustration fits Moriz better than photography.

examples.name: Robb Owen
examples.label: Illustrated avatar + homepage introduction
examples.image: A large outlined avatar in purple and teal sits beside a serif introduction on a very pale background.
examples.copy: The homepage introduction states his name, independent role, and location. The next section explains what he helps people build.
examples.takeaway: Use a custom avatar to make an introduction recognizable, while keeping the role and offer explicit.
examples.fit: Homepage introduction rather than a dedicated About-page capture; useful as a compact section reference.

examples.name: Josh W. Comeau
examples.label: Speaker cutout + personal fact collection
examples.image: A large cutout photograph of Josh speaking sits beside a short introduction on a dark field, above a scalloped transition.
examples.copy: The opening gives career context and current purpose. Short illustrated facts and interactive details provide personality further down.
examples.takeaway: Let one strong portrait anchor the introduction, then separate optional personal facts into small, skimmable pieces.
examples.fit: Useful for playful craft. Interactions below the opening are not needed for a concise homepage bio.

examples.name: Rachel How
examples.label: Large portrait + short current-activity list
examples.image: A large, rounded indoor portrait leads a narrow reading column; additional photographs break up the longer page.
examples.copy: The opening explains what she does now in short linked entries. Selected features and a chronological personal story follow.
examples.takeaway: Use short, specific statements about current work before asking visitors to read a longer biography.
examples.fit: Useful for a multidisciplinary introduction with several current activities.

examples.name: Gloria Lo
examples.label: Text-first opening + wide portrait
examples.image: A simple heading and two introductory paragraphs sit above a large outdoor portrait in a centered column.
examples.copy: The biography explains motivation and a self-taught path. Separate values sections extend the personal story.
examples.takeaway: A clear reading order can work without a side-by-side layout: introduction first, portrait second, values afterward.
examples.fit: Useful for a straightforward stacked layout; shorten the introduction for a compact section.

examples.name: Tobias van Schneider
examples.label: Oversized biography + cinematic portrait
examples.image: Large introductory typography leads into a broad black-and-white outdoor portrait, followed by a longer career narrative.
examples.copy: A third-person introduction establishes a multidisciplinary identity. The following story explains his route into design and independent products.
examples.takeaway: Use image scale and typography to establish an editorial voice; keep the essential introduction readable before the longer story.
examples.fit: Useful for visual confidence. A full biography is better suited to a dedicated page.

examples.name: Alice Lee / itsalicelee
examples.label: Bright portrait + compact personal statement
examples.image: A cheerful portrait against a saturated yellow background anchors an otherwise quiet white layout with pink accents.
examples.copy: A brief personality-led statement introduces her role and origin; contact, achievements, and experience are arranged below.
examples.takeaway: A strongly art-directed portrait can carry the personality while the text stays concise and structured.
examples.fit: This is a different designer from byalicelee and Alice Seohyun Lee; useful for a bolder portrait treatment.

examples.name: Kristina Champion
examples.label: Restrained layout + colorful portrait
examples.image: A vertical portrait with a vivid pink outfit sits beside a long text column in a minimal white composition.
examples.copy: The opening describes experience and product focus. Separate working-style and values sections explain how she collaborates.
examples.takeaway: Make the working relationship tangible: describe how you collaborate, make decisions, and handle complexity.
examples.fit: Useful content reference for professional credibility; a homepage version should be much shorter.

examples.name: Andrew Neyer
examples.label: Wide portrait + creative point of view
examples.image: A wide portrait with a bright yellow beret is followed by a concise identity line and a two-column statement-and-manifesto area.
examples.copy: The page explains his evolving creative practice and point of view, then offers short and long versions of his story.
examples.takeaway: Introduce a recognizable creative belief before supplying a full history; let visitors choose how far to read.
examples.fit: Artist portfolio and product-shop hybrid; useful for personality and editorial hierarchy.

examples.name: Devon Stank
examples.label: Environmental image + personal facts
examples.image: The captured subsection pairs a large city photograph with personal facts on black. The page also opens with a full-bleed working portrait.
examples.copy: Personal interests establish an informal tone before a longer account of discovering development and becoming independent.
examples.takeaway: Use a small set of distinctive personal details to complement the professional story, with imagery that establishes a real setting.
examples.fit: The saved crop shows a contextual photograph, not a headshot; useful for an informal supporting subsection.

examples.name: Sarah Drasner
examples.label: Small portrait over atmospheric imagery
examples.image: A small monochrome portrait and biography panel appear over a full-width city-at-dusk photograph.
examples.copy: A third-person biography summarizes leadership, teaching, speaking, and writing, ending with a short personal aside.
examples.takeaway: A secondary image can set a mood while a smaller portrait identifies the person; protect text legibility with a solid panel.
examples.fit: Atmosphere reference. The captured text is dense and subdued, so simplify copy and increase contrast in an adaptation.
